guides.name: Smart TV
guides.summary: Review voice features, viewing data, and ad choices.
guides.cardDescription: Review voice controls, viewing data, and personalized advertising.

sources.label: FTC: Securing your internet-connected devices at home

steps.title: Microphones & voice assistants
steps.purpose: Understand which voice features are available and decide when they can be used.
instructions: Check the product manual and any paired remote for microphones or voice assistant features. Do not assume a microphone is present.
If supported, review the physical mute switch and voice activation controls. Choose the options that suit your household.
Record anything you cannot verify as unresolved.
steps.tradeoff: Disabling voice features may prevent hands-free commands or voice search.

steps.title: Voice recordings & history
steps.purpose: Review whether a linked account stores voice interactions.
instructions: If your device uses a voice assistant, open its companion app or account privacy controls.
Look for options to review or delete voice history and manage future storage.
If no voice assistant is used, mark this check not applicable.
steps.tradeoff: Deleting history may reduce personalization; account controls may need an internet connection.

steps.title: Usage & diagnostic data
steps.purpose: Make an informed choice about optional usage reporting.
instructions: Check the device settings and manual for diagnostics, analytics, or usage reporting.
Read what each available option shares and disable optional reporting if you prefer.
If you cannot find or verify a control, record it as unresolved.
steps.tradeoff: Optional diagnostics may help the manufacturer troubleshoot problems. Some necessary service data may still be processed.

steps.title: Advertising & personalization
steps.purpose: Review how activity is used for personalized advertising.
instructions: Look for advertising preferences in device settings and linked accounts.
Review personalized ads, advertising identifiers, and any available reset options.
On smart TVs, also look for viewing information or automatic content recognition controls in the manual.
steps.tradeoff: Turning off personalization does not remove advertisements or necessarily stop all data collection.

steps.title: Connected devices & accessories
steps.purpose: Understand the capabilities of accessories connected to this device.
instructions: Review paired remotes, speakers, headphones, and other accessories.
Check each accessory’s documentation for microphone capabilities. Record unknown capabilities in your notes.
Remove pairings you no longer use and review discovery options where available.
steps.tradeoff: Removing pairings stops those accessories from connecting until paired again.

steps.title: Companion app permissions
steps.purpose: Limit app access to information and features you do not need.
instructions: Open your phone or tablet settings for the device’s companion app.
Review microphone, location, contacts, and nearby-device permissions.
Turn off optional access you do not need and check that your essential features still work.
steps.tradeoff: Some permissions may be needed for initial setup, discovery, or specific app features.

steps.title: Updates & a final review
steps.purpose: Keep a record of your choices and revisit them after updates.
instructions: Check the manufacturer’s instructions for software updates.
After an update, revisit your privacy choices and note any changed controls.
Export a backup of your checklist so you have a copy outside this browser.
steps.tradeoff: Updates may change menus and available options. A completed checklist is a record of your review, not a privacy guarantee.

guides.name: Smart speaker
guides.summary: Review voice features, recordings, accounts, and app access.
guides.cardDescription: Understand microphones, voice history, and connected accounts.

sources.label: FTC: Securing your internet-connected devices at home
FTC: How to secure your voice assistant and protect your privacy

steps.title: Voice assistant & microphone
steps.purpose: Check whether this speaker has a microphone or voice assistant before changing its controls.
instructions: Check the speaker and its documentation for a microphone, voice button, or wake word. Presence and controls vary by model.
If supported, review mute and voice activation controls and choose the settings you prefer.
If you cannot confirm the capability, mark it unresolved.
steps.tradeoff: Muting the microphone or disabling voice control can turn off hands-free requests.

steps.title: Voice recordings & history
steps.purpose: Review what a linked assistant account may retain.
instructions: Identify which voice assistant account is connected, if any.
Use that assistant’s official privacy controls to review recording history, deletion, and future storage options.
If no assistant is connected or the feature is absent, mark this not applicable.
steps.tradeoff: Deleting history may reduce personalization and may require access to the assistant account.

steps.title: Linked accounts & services
steps.purpose: Limit the services and personal information connected to the speaker.
instructions: Review music, shopping, home-control, and other linked services in the companion app.
Remove services or household profiles you no longer use.
Check the privacy controls of each service separately; they may have their own retention settings.
steps.tradeoff: Removing a service can disable its voice commands or personalized features.

steps.title: Diagnostics & usage data
steps.purpose: Review optional device performance and usage reporting.
instructions: Check the device manual and settings for diagnostics, analytics, or usage reporting.
Read the available choices and turn off optional reporting if you prefer.
Record controls you cannot find as unresolved.
steps.tradeoff: Optional diagnostics can help troubleshoot issues; essential service data may still be processed.

steps.title: Connected accessories
steps.purpose: Check microphones and access on paired devices.
instructions: Review phones, tablets, remotes, or other devices paired with the speaker.
Check each accessory’s manual for its own microphone and voice controls.
Remove old pairings you no longer use.
steps.tradeoff: Removing a pairing means you will need to pair that accessory again to use it.

steps.title: Companion app permissions
steps.purpose: Limit what the phone app can access.
instructions: Open your phone’s settings for the speaker’s companion app.
Review microphone, nearby-device, contacts, and location permissions.
Turn off access you do not need, then check the features you rely on.
steps.tradeoff: Setup, discovery, calling, or location features may need specific permissions.

steps.title: Updates & privacy review
steps.purpose: Revisit your choices after software or app updates.
instructions: Check the manufacturer’s update guidance.
After an update, review voice, account, and data-sharing settings again.
Save a note of anything that changed.
steps.tradeoff: Menus and options can change with software updates; this checklist is a record of your review, not a privacy guarantee.

guides.name: Streaming device
guides.summary: Review account activity, ads, apps, and connections.
guides.cardDescription: Take a closer look at ad preferences, app permissions, and usage data.

sources.label: FTC: Securing your internet-connected devices at home

steps.title: Remote voice search & microphones
steps.purpose: Determine whether this streaming device or remote supports voice input.
instructions: Check the remote and device manual for a microphone or voice-search button. Do not assume one is present.
If supported, review voice activation controls and what account receives voice requests.
If absent or unverified, record not applicable or unresolved as appropriate.
steps.tradeoff: Disabling voice search may mean using the on-screen keyboard or app remote.

steps.title: Viewing & usage information
steps.purpose: Review optional viewing, diagnostics, and recommendation data.
instructions: Look in device settings and the manufacturer’s privacy documentation for viewing activity, usage data, and diagnostics.
Review available controls for activity-based recommendations or optional reporting.
Record options that are unavailable or unclear.
steps.tradeoff: Disabling activity-based recommendations may make suggestions less personalized; it does not necessarily stop all data processing.

steps.title: Advertising preferences
steps.purpose: Review ad personalization and advertising identifiers where offered.
instructions: Check settings on the streaming device and its linked account.
Review personalized advertising or advertising identifier controls if available.
Keep in mind that turning off personalization may not remove ads.
steps.tradeoff: Ads may continue to appear, and a reset identifier does not necessarily stop all collection.

steps.title: Account & profile privacy
steps.purpose: Check account profiles and viewing history.
instructions: Review which account and profiles are signed in on this device.
Remove profiles you no longer need and use the provider’s controls to review viewing history.
Use official account privacy settings for retention and activity controls.
steps.tradeoff: Removing a profile or clearing history may affect recommendations and access on this device.

steps.title: Installed app permissions
steps.purpose: Review information available to apps on the streaming device.
instructions: Review installed apps and the permissions or data-sharing choices the device exposes.
Remove apps you no longer use.
For account-level privacy and retention, consult each app provider’s official controls.
steps.tradeoff: Removing an app or limiting its access can disable its features until you reinstall or sign in again.

steps.title: Casting & device connections
steps.purpose: Review how phones and other household devices can connect.
instructions: Check settings for casting, device discovery, remote-app connections, and guest access.
Disable discovery options you do not use and remove old paired devices.
Confirm the controls in your model’s manual.
steps.tradeoff: Disabling discovery may prevent phones or smart-home devices from finding the streamer.

steps.title: Updates & a final review
steps.purpose: Recheck privacy choices when the device software changes.
instructions: Check how the manufacturer delivers software updates.
After an update, review account, advertising, app, and connection settings.
Record unresolved questions for later.
steps.tradeoff: Updates may move or change settings. A completed checklist does not certify a device as private.

guides.name: Soundbar
guides.summary: Review voice features, accessories, app access, and updates.
guides.cardDescription: Review voice features, paired accessories, and connectivity.

sources.label: FTC: Securing your internet-connected devices at home
FTC: How to secure your voice assistant and protect your privacy

steps.title: Voice features & microphones
steps.purpose: Check whether the soundbar itself or its remote supports voice input.
instructions: Review the soundbar and remote documentation for microphones, wake words, or voice assistant support.
If available, locate mute and voice activation controls.
Check connected devices separately; an attached TV may have its own voice features.
steps.tradeoff: Disabling voice controls can remove hands-free commands or voice search.

steps.title: Voice assistant history
steps.purpose: Review account storage when a voice assistant is connected.
instructions: Identify any voice assistant linked to the soundbar or a connected TV.
Review recording history and retention in the assistant provider’s official account controls.
If no assistant is connected, mark this not applicable.
steps.tradeoff: Deleting history may change personalization and must often be done through the linked account.

steps.title: Paired devices & microphones
steps.purpose: Understand what paired remotes, phones, and accessories can do.
instructions: Review Bluetooth pairings and other connected audio accessories.
Check each accessory’s documentation for microphones and voice controls.
Remove unused pairings and note any capability you cannot verify.
steps.tradeoff: Removing a pairing stops automatic connection until you pair the accessory again.

steps.title: Diagnostics & usage data
steps.purpose: Review optional product diagnostics and usage reporting.
instructions: Look in the manual, companion app, and device settings for diagnostics or analytics controls.
Review what is shared and turn off optional reporting if you prefer.
If no control is documented, mark the step unresolved rather than assuming.
steps.tradeoff: Optional reporting may help troubleshoot audio issues; service data may still be processed.

steps.title: Companion app permissions
steps.purpose: Limit the soundbar app’s access on your phone.
instructions: Open your phone settings for the soundbar’s companion app.
Review nearby-device, microphone, contacts, and location permissions.
Turn off access you do not need and check the features you use.
steps.tradeoff: Pairing, room calibration, voice setup, or discovery may depend on certain permissions.

steps.title: Network & connected services
steps.purpose: Review network access and services linked to the soundbar.
instructions: Check which network and streaming or voice services are connected.
Remove accounts and services you no longer use.
Review privacy choices with each connected service provider.
steps.tradeoff: Disconnecting a service or network can disable streaming, remote control, or software updates.

steps.title: Updates & a final review
steps.purpose: Revisit soundbar privacy choices after firmware changes.
instructions: Check the manufacturer’s instructions for firmware updates.
After an update, review voice, pairing, app, and network choices.
Record settings that moved or changed.
steps.tradeoff: Menus can change after updates. This checklist records your review; it does not certify a device.

guides.name: Headphones & Bluetooth
guides.summary: Review microphones, pairings, app access, and device finding.
guides.cardDescription: Check microphones, paired devices, and companion app access.

sources.label: FTC: Securing your internet-connected devices at home
FTC: How to secure your voice assistant and protect your privacy

steps.title: Microphone & voice assistant
steps.purpose: Check how headset microphones and voice assistants are activated.
instructions: Review the headphones’ manual for microphone, voice assistant, and call controls.
Check both headset buttons and phone voice-assistant settings.
If you cannot verify when the microphone is active, record that question.
steps.tradeoff: Disabling voice activation can remove hands-free assistant commands; the microphone may still work for calls.

steps.title: Voice assistant history
steps.purpose: Review retention through the phone or assistant account.
instructions: If the headphones invoke a phone or cloud voice assistant, identify the account that handles requests.
Review history and deletion controls in that provider’s official privacy settings.
If no assistant is used, mark this not applicable.
steps.tradeoff: History controls are usually managed by the connected phone or account, not the headphones.

steps.title: Companion app permissions
steps.purpose: Limit the headphone app’s access to your phone data.
instructions: Open your phone settings for the headphone companion app.
Review nearby-device, location, microphone, contacts, and motion permissions if listed.
Disable permissions you do not need and check pairing and audio features.
steps.tradeoff: Some permissions may support setup, device finding, or optional sound features.

steps.title: Bluetooth pairing & discovery
steps.purpose: Keep track of devices that can connect to the headphones.
instructions: Review saved Bluetooth pairings on your phone and other devices.
Remove devices you no longer use and check whether the headphones have a pairing or discoverability mode.
Use the manual to understand how pairing mode is activated.
steps.tradeoff: Removing a device means you must pair it again before it can play audio.

steps.title: Diagnostics & product usage
steps.purpose: Review optional product analytics and diagnostic sharing.
instructions: Check the companion app and manufacturer privacy notice for diagnostics, crash reports, or usage analytics.
Review available choices and disable optional reporting if you prefer.
If no choice is offered, note that rather than assuming sharing is off.
steps.tradeoff: Optional diagnostics may help improve or troubleshoot the product.

steps.title: Location & device-finding features
steps.purpose: Understand any location access or find-my-device feature.
instructions: Check whether the app offers a last-seen location or device-finding feature.
Review the app’s location permission and your phone’s location history controls.
If no location feature exists, mark the step not applicable.
steps.tradeoff: Turning off location can disable device-finding features; phone operating systems may retain their own location records.

steps.title: Firmware & app updates
steps.purpose: Revisit controls after headphone firmware or companion app updates.
instructions: Check the manufacturer’s update guidance and whether updates use the companion app.
After an update, review permissions, voice, pairing, and diagnostics settings again.
Record any changed controls or unresolved questions.
steps.tradeoff: Updates can change menus or features. A completed checklist is not a privacy certification.

guides.name: Wi-Fi router & home hub
guides.summary: Review administrator access, connected devices, remote access, and updates.
guides.cardDescription: Check who can manage your network, which devices connect, and what is shared.

sources.label: FTC: Securing your internet-connected devices at home
CISA: 5 steps to protecting your digital home

steps.title: Administrator access
steps.purpose: Keep router management limited to people you trust.
instructions: Review administrator accounts and remove old or unused access.
Change any default administrator password using the router’s official instructions.
Use a unique password and enable stronger sign-in protection if offered.
steps.tradeoff: Anyone with administrator access may be able to change network settings or view connected devices.

steps.title: Connected devices & guests
steps.purpose: Know which devices and visitors use your network.
instructions: Review the connected-device list and identify unfamiliar entries before taking action.
Remove access for devices you no longer use.
Review guest network access and turn it off when it is not needed.
steps.tradeoff: Removing a device may interrupt its connection until you add it again.

steps.title: Remote management & cloud accounts
steps.purpose: Understand whether router controls are available away from home.
instructions: Check whether a cloud account or remote-management feature is enabled.
Review who can sign in to that account and remove access you no longer need.
Disable remote access if you do not use it, following the router’s instructions.
steps.tradeoff: Remote management can be useful when away from home but adds another way to reach network settings.

steps.title: Network logs & diagnostics
steps.purpose: Review what activity and performance data the router keeps or shares.
instructions: Look for diagnostics, usage reports, traffic history, or analytics in settings and documentation.
Review available choices and disable optional sharing if you prefer.
Record features you cannot verify instead of assuming they are off.
steps.tradeoff: Turning off optional reports may limit troubleshooting information; basic service data may still be processed.

steps.title: Wi-Fi security & sharing
steps.purpose: Check how your network is protected and shared.
instructions: Use the manufacturer’s guidance to review the current Wi-Fi security mode.
Review saved network access and change the Wi-Fi password if it has been shared widely.
Check whether device discovery or local sharing features are enabled.
steps.tradeoff: Changing Wi-Fi settings can disconnect household devices until they reconnect.

steps.title: DNS & filtering services
steps.purpose: Understand services that can see or filter network requests.
instructions: Check whether the router uses a custom DNS provider, parental controls, or filtering service.
Review the provider and account settings for data-retention information.
Change these options only if you understand how they affect browsing and household controls.
steps.tradeoff: Changing DNS or filtering can affect access, safety filters, and network troubleshooting.

steps.title: Firmware & app updates
steps.purpose: Keep a record of router updates and revisit important choices afterward.
instructions: Check how the manufacturer announces and installs router updates.
Review automatic update and notification options.
After a firmware update, revisit administrator, remote-access, and sharing settings.
steps.tradeoff: Updates may move settings or change features; the checklist records your review and does not certify security.

guides.name: Smart camera & doorbell
guides.summary: Review recording, storage, sharing, motion features, and app access.
guides.cardDescription: Understand recording controls, account sharing, notifications, and storage.

sources.label: FTC: Securing your internet-connected devices at home
FTC: How to secure your home security cameras

steps.title: Recording & activity zones
steps.purpose: Choose when the camera records and which areas it covers.
instructions: Review motion, sound, and continuous-recording options in the app.
Check activity or privacy zones and exclude areas you do not want monitored.
Confirm whether the camera has a physical privacy shutter or indicator.
steps.tradeoff: Reducing recording can mean missing events you wanted the camera to capture.

steps.title: Video storage & retention
steps.purpose: Find out where recordings are stored and how long they remain available.
instructions: Check whether clips are stored locally, with a subscription, or in a cloud account.
Review automatic deletion and retention settings.
Use the provider’s official controls to delete clips you no longer need.
steps.tradeoff: Shorter retention or local-only storage may limit access to older clips or remote playback.

steps.title: Household sharing
steps.purpose: Limit who can see live video, recordings, or camera controls.
instructions: Review household members, shared users, and active sessions.
Remove access for people who no longer need it.
Check whether shared users can view recordings, change settings, or invite others.
steps.tradeoff: Removing a shared user also removes their viewing and control access.

steps.title: Microphone, audio & other sensors
steps.purpose: Check which sensors the camera uses, beyond video.
instructions: Review microphone, speaker, sound detection, and any other sensor features.
Turn off audio or sensor features you do not need, where controls are offered.
Check for a physical control and note anything you cannot verify.
steps.tradeoff: Disabling audio or detection features may reduce alerts or two-way communication.

steps.title: Motion alerts & notifications
steps.purpose: Choose which activity produces an alert and where alerts appear.
instructions: Review motion and sound detection sensitivity and schedules.
Check whether alerts include preview images or other details on your phone’s lock screen.
Limit notifications to events and times that are useful to you.
steps.tradeoff: Fewer alerts can reduce interruptions but may mean you notice an event later.

steps.title: Connected services & voice assistants
steps.purpose: Review other apps or services that can access the camera.
instructions: Check linked voice assistants, smart-home services, and automation integrations.
Remove connections you no longer use.
Review each linked service’s account and video-history controls separately.
steps.tradeoff: Disconnecting a service can stop routines, voice commands, or shared notifications.

steps.title: App, account & firmware review
steps.purpose: Recheck camera privacy choices after app or firmware changes.
instructions: Review app permissions for camera management on your phone.
Check for firmware and companion-app updates using official channels.
After updates, revisit recording, sharing, and storage choices.
steps.tradeoff: Updates can change menus and features; a completed checklist is not a privacy guarantee.

guides.name: Smart display
guides.summary: Review camera and microphone controls, accounts, sensors, and sharing.
guides.cardDescription: Check voice and camera controls, connected accounts, and ambient features.

sources.label: FTC: Securing your internet-connected devices at home
FTC: How to secure your voice assistant and protect your privacy

steps.title: Camera & physical privacy controls
steps.purpose: Understand when the display’s camera can be used.
instructions: Check the manual for camera, shutter, indicator-light, and video-call features.
Review app and account settings for camera use and sharing.
Use a physical shutter or disable the camera when you do not need it, if available.
steps.tradeoff: Disabling the camera may prevent video calls or camera-based features.

steps.title: Microphone & voice activation
steps.purpose: Choose how voice features listen and respond.
instructions: Review microphone mute, wake-word, and voice activation controls.
Check whether the display has a hardware mute switch and how it signals mute.
If the display is linked to an assistant, review that account’s voice settings too.
steps.tradeoff: Muting voice features may disable hands-free commands and voice search.

steps.title: Presence, gestures & ambient sensing
steps.purpose: Check for sensors that detect people, movement, or the room.
instructions: Review presence detection, gesture control, ambient light, and sleep or wake features.
Disable sensing features you do not use if the display provides controls.
Note when sensing happens and whether the device offers a visible indicator.
steps.tradeoff: Disabling sensors may affect automatic screen, brightness, or room-aware features.

steps.title: Profiles, photos & personal content
steps.purpose: Review what personal accounts and content appear on the display.
instructions: Check signed-in profiles, photo libraries, calendars, and other personal services.
Remove accounts or content sources you no longer use.
Review shared household access and the display’s lock or personal-results options.
steps.tradeoff: Removing an account may also remove personalized content or household features.

steps.title: Connected devices & services
steps.purpose: Limit the services that can send information to or through the display.
instructions: Review linked smart-home devices, voice services, and third-party apps.
Remove connections that are no longer useful.
Check privacy and retention controls in each linked service.
steps.tradeoff: Disconnecting a service may stop routines, casting, or voice control for those devices.

steps.title: Companion app & notifications
steps.purpose: Limit access through the phone app and notification previews.
instructions: Review the companion app’s microphone, camera, nearby-device, and location permissions.
Check whether notifications show personal information on the display or phone lock screen.
Turn off permissions or previews you do not need and test the features you use.
steps.tradeoff: Some permissions are needed for setup, calling, casting, or device discovery.

steps.title: Updates & a final review
steps.purpose: Keep the display’s software current and revisit privacy choices.
instructions: Check the manufacturer’s official update instructions.
After updates, review camera, microphone, account, sensing, and app controls.
Record any changed settings or questions.
steps.tradeoff: Updates may move controls; this checklist records your review but does not verify a specific model.

guides.name: Smart thermostat
guides.summary: Review occupancy sensing, location features, accounts, and data sharing.
guides.cardDescription: Check what occupancy and location features reveal about your routines.

sources.label: FTC: Securing your internet-connected devices at home
CISA: 5 steps to protecting your digital home

steps.title: Schedules & occupancy patterns
steps.purpose: Understand what your schedule may reveal about household routines.
instructions: Review programmed schedules, away modes, and occupancy-based changes.
Remove old schedules or locations you no longer use.
Choose a schedule that shares only the routine information you are comfortable storing.
steps.tradeoff: Schedules can reveal when a home is usually occupied and affect comfort or energy use.

steps.title: Location & geofencing
steps.purpose: Check whether phone location changes thermostat behavior.
instructions: Review location permission for the thermostat app on each phone.
Check whether geofencing or arrival and departure automation is enabled.
Disable location-based features you do not use and confirm the home schedule still works.
steps.tradeoff: Turning off location features may stop automatic away or arrival adjustments.

steps.title: Presence & environmental sensors
steps.purpose: Review sensors used to adjust heating or cooling.
instructions: Check for room sensors, occupancy detection, humidity, and other environmental readings.
Review how readings are used and whether optional sensing features can be disabled.
Remove or rename sensors you no longer use.
steps.tradeoff: Changing sensor use can affect comfort, room balancing, or automatic adjustments.

steps.title: Household & installer access
steps.purpose: Keep thermostat control with people who need it.
instructions: Review household members, invited users, installer access, and active sessions.
Remove access that is no longer needed.
Check whether guests can view schedules, change settings, or invite other users.
steps.tradeoff: Removing access prevents those people from changing temperature or schedules.

steps.title: Voice & smart-home connections
steps.purpose: Review other services that can read or control the thermostat.
instructions: Check connected voice assistants, home platforms, and automation services.
Remove integrations you no longer use.
Review privacy controls for the linked accounts separately.
steps.tradeoff: Disconnecting services may disable voice control and automated routines.

steps.title: Usage, energy & diagnostic data
steps.purpose: Understand reports about device use and energy patterns.
instructions: Review energy reports, diagnostics, and product-improvement settings.
Check whether reports are tied to your account or shared with other services.
Disable optional reporting if you prefer and record unavailable controls.
steps.tradeoff: Turning off optional reports may reduce energy insights or troubleshooting help.

steps.title: Updates & account review
steps.purpose: Revisit thermostat controls after updates or service changes.
instructions: Check official firmware and companion-app update guidance.
Review app permissions and account security.
After updates, revisit schedules, location, sharing, and sensor choices.
steps.tradeoff: Updates can change menus and automatic behavior; the checklist is not model-specific.

guides.name: Smart lighting
guides.summary: Review app access, schedules, integrations, and connected accounts.
guides.cardDescription: Check who can control your lights and which services are connected.

sources.label: FTC: Securing your internet-connected devices at home
CISA: 5 steps to protecting your digital home

steps.title: App access & household members
steps.purpose: Know who can control the lights or view their state.
instructions: Review users and households in the lighting app or hub.
Remove people and old accounts that no longer need access.
Check whether invited users can add more users or connect services.
steps.tradeoff: Removing access stops those people from controlling the lights through the app.

steps.title: Schedules, scenes & occupancy
steps.purpose: Review automation that can reveal when rooms are in use.
instructions: Check schedules, presence-based routines, vacation mode, and motion sensors.
Remove routines you no longer use and review when they run.
Disable occupancy features you do not need, where controls are available.
steps.tradeoff: Changing automations may affect convenience, security routines, or energy use.

steps.title: Voice assistants & home platforms
steps.purpose: Limit connected services that can control the lighting system.
instructions: Review voice assistants, home platforms, and third-party integrations.
Remove services you no longer use.
Check the linked account’s privacy and voice-history controls separately.
steps.tradeoff: Disconnecting an integration may stop voice commands or cross-device routines.

steps.title: Connectivity & pairing
steps.purpose: Keep track of the hub and devices that join the lighting system.
instructions: Review paired bulbs, switches, bridges, and remote access.
Remove devices that are no longer part of your home setup.
Check whether pairing mode or guest access remains enabled when not in use.
steps.tradeoff: Removing a pairing means you may need to reset or reconnect that device later.

steps.title: Companion app permissions
steps.purpose: Limit phone access granted to the lighting app.
instructions: Review nearby-device, Bluetooth, local network, microphone, and location permissions if listed.
Turn off access not needed for the features you use.
Test discovery, setup, and remote-control features afterward.
steps.tradeoff: Setup and local discovery may rely on nearby-device or network permissions.

steps.title: Diagnostics & usage data
steps.purpose: Review optional reporting from the lighting app or hub.
instructions: Look for diagnostics, analytics, or product-improvement choices.
Read what is shared and turn off optional reporting if you prefer.
Note if the app offers no control or clear description.
steps.tradeoff: Optional diagnostics may help troubleshoot connection and device issues.

steps.title: Updates & a final review
steps.purpose: Recheck connected services and routines after updates.
instructions: Check official app, hub, and firmware update guidance.
Review household access, integrations, schedules, and app permissions after an update.
Record routines or controls that have changed.
steps.tradeoff: Updates can change automation behavior or move menu options.

guides.name: Robot vacuum
guides.summary: Review maps, cameras, app access, sharing, and data retention.
guides.cardDescription: Check stored floor maps, sensors, account sharing, and app access.

sources.label: FTC: Securing your internet-connected devices at home
CISA: 5 steps to protecting your digital home

steps.title: Maps, rooms & floor plans
steps.purpose: Check which maps the vacuum stores and how they are used.
instructions: Review saved maps, room labels, no-go zones, and map backup options.
Delete maps for old homes or maps you no longer need.
Check whether maps sync to an account or remain on the vacuum.
steps.tradeoff: Deleting a map may require a new mapping run and room setup.

steps.title: Cameras, microphones & sensors
steps.purpose: Find out what the vacuum can sense beyond movement.
instructions: Check the manual for camera, microphone, obstacle recognition, and mapping sensors.
Review controls for visual recognition or sensor data collection.
Do not assume a sensor is present or disabled; record anything unverified.
steps.tradeoff: Disabling sensing can reduce obstacle avoidance or navigation features.

steps.title: Account & household sharing
steps.purpose: Limit who can start, locate, or manage the vacuum.
instructions: Review household users, shared accounts, and active sessions.
Remove access for people who no longer need it.
Check whether shared users can see maps, routines, or device location.
steps.tradeoff: Removing access stops that person from controlling the vacuum through the app.

steps.title: Location & device finding
steps.purpose: Review location access and lost-device features.
instructions: Check phone location permission for the companion app.
Review any last-seen location, device-finding, or remote-alert feature.
Turn off location access you do not need and verify what features are affected.
steps.tradeoff: Disabling location may prevent the app from locating a misplaced device.

steps.title: Companion app permissions
steps.purpose: Limit access the vacuum app receives on your phone.
instructions: Review nearby-device, local network, microphone, camera, and location permissions if listed.
Disable permissions that do not support features you use.
Test pairing, scheduling, and remote control afterward.
steps.tradeoff: Permissions may be required for initial setup or local discovery.

steps.title: Cleaning history & diagnostics
steps.purpose: Understand reports about cleaning activity and device performance.
instructions: Review cleaning history, usage analytics, and diagnostic-report settings.
Check whether reports include room names, maps, or timestamps.
Disable optional reporting if available and note unclear controls.
steps.tradeoff: Reducing history or diagnostics can limit cleaning insights and support.

steps.title: Updates & a final review
steps.purpose: Revisit map, sharing, and sensor choices after updates.
instructions: Check official firmware and app update guidance.
After updates, review maps, account sharing, app permissions, and sensing choices.
Record any settings that moved or changed.
steps.tradeoff: Updates may change features; a completed checklist does not verify a specific model.

steps.title: Accounts & household access
steps.purpose: Know who can use the appliance’s app or remote features.
instructions: Review signed-in accounts, invited household members, and active sessions.
Remove access no longer needed.
Check what shared users can view or control.
steps.tradeoff: Removing access may prevent someone from starting or managing appliance cycles.

steps.title: Companion app permissions
steps.purpose: Limit what the appliance app can access on your phone.
instructions: Review nearby-device, local network, Bluetooth, microphone, camera, and location permissions if listed.
Disable permissions you do not need for features you use.
Test setup and remote-control functions afterward.
steps.tradeoff: Some permissions may be necessary for pairing, alerts, or remote operation.

steps.title: Remote start & controls
steps.purpose: Choose whether the appliance can be monitored or started remotely.
instructions: Review remote monitoring, start, and notification options.
Disable remote control when you do not use it or when the appliance should be locally controlled.
Check for a physical control or interlock and follow the manual.
steps.tradeoff: Remote features may be required for alerts, scheduling, or energy programs.

steps.title: Voice services & integrations
steps.purpose: Review services connected to the appliance.
instructions: Check voice assistants, home platforms, retailer services, and other integrations.
Remove connections you no longer use.
Review each linked provider’s privacy controls separately.
steps.tradeoff: Disconnecting a service may stop voice commands or automated routines.

steps.title: Diagnostics & product usage
steps.purpose: Understand what usage information is shared for support or product improvement.
instructions: Look for analytics, diagnostics, maintenance, and product-improvement settings.
Review what is collected and turn off optional sharing if you prefer.
Record controls that are unclear or unavailable.
steps.tradeoff: Optional diagnostics can support maintenance; essential service information may still be processed.

steps.title: Alerts, cameras & voice features
steps.purpose: Check whether the appliance has sensors or captures information around it.
instructions: Review cameras, microphones, voice controls, presence sensors, and notification previews if present.
Check physical indicators or privacy controls in the manual.
Disable features you do not use and note capabilities you cannot verify.
steps.tradeoff: Disabling sensors or alerts may reduce safety, monitoring, or convenience features.

steps.title: Updates & final review
steps.purpose: Keep track of software updates and revisit privacy choices.
instructions: Check official app and firmware update instructions.
After updates, review remote controls, sharing, app permissions, and diagnostics.
Record changes or unresolved questions.
steps.tradeoff: Updates can change menus and features; this checklist is not a model-specific certification.
